title: Mitochondrial complex IV disruption is a detrimental pathology conferring ssusceptibility to alzheimer’s disease
title_zh: 线粒体复合体IV的破坏是导致阿尔茨海默病易感性的有害病理改变
abstract: Abstract Mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) is an integral part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) and plays a pivotal role in maintaining mitochondrial function. In contrast to the long-standing recognition of its dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), the exact role of CIV deficit in the pathogenesis of this neurodegenerative disorder remains poorly defined. In this study, by incorporating clinical resources, mouse- and human-based models of AD risk, and a genetic approach to bypass defective CIV via the ectopic expression of alternative oxidase (AOX), we examined whether CIV deficits are a pathogenic driver of or a beneficial adaptation to AD-associated pathologies. Our results showed a clinicopathological association between neuronal CIV dysfunction and pathological characteristics of AD. Further experiments linked defective CIV to the development of mitochondrial dysfunction and synaptic loss in the tested mouse- and human-based models of AD risk. In addition, a reciprocal relationship between CIV dysfunction and amyloid pathology was determined. Lastly, a proteome-wide association study (PWAS) using genetic data from large-scale AD cohorts identified that downregulation of COX11, a crucial CIV assembly factor, confers susceptibility to AD risk. Collectively, our findings suggest that CIV dysfunction is a detrimental pathology contributing to AD-associated mitochondrial and neuronal damage. The dual role of CIV dysfunction, both as a consequence of and a contributor to amyloid toxicity in AD pathogenesis, further justifies the therapeutic potential of strategies targeting CIV deficits to diversify the tools for prevention and treatment of this neurodegenerative disorder.
abstract_zh: 摘要 线粒体复合体IV（CIV）是线粒体电子传递链（ETC）的重要组成部分，在维持线粒体功能中起关键作用。尽管人们长期以来认识到其在阿尔茨海默病（AD）中的功能障碍，但CIV缺陷在该神经退行性疾病病理机制中的确切作用仍知之甚少。在本研究中，通过整合临床资源、小鼠和人类的AD风险模型，以及通过异源表达替代氧化酶（AOX）来绕过缺陷CIV的遗传方法，我们检查了CIV缺陷是阿尔茨海默病相关病理的致病驱动因素还是有益的适应。结果显示，神经元CIV功能障碍与AD的病理特征之间存在临床病理学关联。进一步实验将缺陷CIV与测试中小鼠和人类AD风险模型中的线粒体功能障碍和突触丧失联系起来。此外，确定了CIV功能障碍与淀粉样蛋白病理之间的相互关系。最后，利用大规模AD队列的遗传数据进行全基因组关联研究（PWAS），确定COX11的下调——这是CIV组装的关键因子——使个体易患AD风险。综上所述，我们的研究结果表明，CIV功能障碍是导致AD相关线粒体和神经元损伤的有害病理。CIV功能障碍在阿尔茨海默病病理机制中既是后果又是淀粉样毒性的贡献者，这一双重角色进一步证明了针对CIV缺陷的治疗策略在预防和治疗这种神经退行性疾病方面的潜力。
